steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Govno... govno, govno, govno!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Where did those casters come from?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why can't the guns kill them or even aim at them? Blyat, what are they—

spans.text: Why can't the guns kill them or even aim at them?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Anatoliy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Oh, Hierda—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hierda!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: There you are. No, why are you here? Didn't I instruct for you to evacuate first?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: It's not safe here. I'll come and find you once I retake Zelgrad. Now, go to the base where my mother is—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I'm not going, Anatoliy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...Even you defy me now?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: No, it's not that. I respect your authority and your decision. But did you forget what we talked about?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You want me to return to your mother's side, even send me away first...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Who will protect you if I'm gone?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: My battleship, my glorious soldiers of Ursus—they still hold their ground! Many of them are cowards, but they make good enough cannon fodder.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I'll make Zelgrad great again and prove myself to Mother once I clear those fleeing pests out of Zelgrad—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Prove that I'm worthy of her name.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Anatoliy...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I can't always watch over you on the battlefield. Even though you're not by my side, your protection is always with me, isn't it?
The young man smiles childishly as he points to the golden rocks on his body. Somehow, they have been growing in number.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You told your guards to escort me back to base, but your mother is already leaving it to go to the border.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Marshal Svetlana Ulyanova is abandoning you and Zelgrad. She doesn't even want to stay at the base near Zelgrad anymore.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: There's still time to come with me, Anatoliy—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Time to catch up to your mother's fleet... to get an answer.

steps.name: Runner
steps.text: The Generalik has reached the base safely. We are ready to depart.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Good. We depart as soon as all units are ready.

steps.name: Runner
steps.text: Yes, Your High Excellency.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Anatoliy.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I can tell by your footsteps.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You can tell it was me, yet you do not even turn. Do you not want to see my face anymore?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I must say that I am disappointed by your actions in Zelgrad.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Why did you not obey my order to retreat?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: That's what I want to ask you... Mother.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why did you abandon Zelgrad? Why did you leave it to the rebels, when you had promised me the city?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: We have gained everything we need from Project Zero. The city itself is worthless.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Our priority is to evacuate with the fruits of the research.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Unbelievable... they were telling the truth...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You have betrayed Ursus.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I'm protecting the First Army, and you.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Grypherburg is the epicenter of strife and intrigue right now. With the fruits of Project Zero in our hands, we'd be putting a target on our backs if we took a side.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I had hoped that you would understand this.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Aren't we glorious soldiers of Ursus? Aren't we fighting for the glory of Ursus?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I swore that I would bring down every last one of the empire's foes!

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Enough. You're not in a good place. I'll have someone take over your mission. Go to your room and get some rest.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: There will come a day when I leave everything to you, Anatoliy... I only hope that when that day comes, you will not be as juvenile as you are today.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I don't understand... I don't even know who I am, Mother.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I'm not a glorious soldier of Ursus, I'm not an Infected, I'm not a pure-blood noble, I'm not even sure if I'm alive...

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Enough! No more such talk—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why... why do you despise me so...?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Is it because I'm the son of a failure?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: ...No, Anatoliy, whatever the reasons I might be angry with you, your blood is not one of them.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: This is the one thing that you never had any choice in.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: But you don't deny that I share his blood.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Does it matter?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Does it not?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Anatoliy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I'm sure I must have gone mad, Mother.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Ugh—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: It doesn't matter? How could it not matter? How else can I explain to myself—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Explain your indulgence and exploitation, your pampering and disinterest?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You never saw me as a son! I've only ever been an object, an object that needed no education, a tool for drawing attention!

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: *cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: No... that's not true—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Then what am I, Mother?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Something that can be cast aside at any moment... right?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Tolya, my child—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You're driving me mad.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Ah... so your blood runs hot too...

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Ugh... argh—

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Tolya, no...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why couldn't I just be your son, a son you could be proud of?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I don't understand... why do things have to be so complicated?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Our previous campaigns were like picnics compared to the pace we're making right now.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: This is what a high-speed battleship is like... max speed is usually not achievable in combat scenarios, but now—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Let's see what you can do.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Unknown assault ship...

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: This is Fourth Army Command. Identify yourself.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: ...It might be the Volnov...

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Repeat, identify yourself.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Thirty.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Stay on course.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Unknown ship, you are approaching a frigate of the Fourth Army. Identify yourself.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: This is your first warning. Identify yourself immediately to prove that you are not hostile and that you have not been hijacked.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: The target is not slowing down.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Have deck artillery on standby.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Forty-two.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Continue.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Unknown ship, this is your second warning. Identify yourself immediately.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: The assault ship is on a direct course for the frigate, the only thing standing between it and the flagship.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Deck artillery standing by.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Fifty-five.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Steady.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Unknown ship, you have entered a restricted area. Identify yourself immediately!

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Under fifty klicks.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Artillery positions, begin tracking target.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Maintain radio silence.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Unknown ship, this is your final warning! Identify yourself immediately!

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Thirty klicks.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Get a firing solution.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Seventy-eight.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Steady as she goes.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Twenty klicks!

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Unknown ship, you are now within firing range!

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Open fire. Disable the ship, but do not destroy it.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Keep firing.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Ninety-one.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Stay on course.

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: ...Blyat, it's the Volnov... why is it still accelerating?

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Keep firing!

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: ...Bzzt...

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: ...Confirm hit—

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Confirm speed...

steps.name: Comms Voice
steps.text: Crazy zhopa!

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Stop your reckless action now, Scioppa Razin, and I will forgive Sechin's previous transgressions.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Take your men and return to your station.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Pfft...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I gotta give you credit. You're trying to negotiate, even when the other side's practically shitting on your face.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Don't worry, I'm just here to return the Volnov.

spans.text: Don't worry, I'm just here to return the

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Besides, Sechin's no longer part of the Fourth Army, as of yesterday.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Any more stupid questions?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Mudak! You absolute fool—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: First zhopa, now mudak. Well, I guess I'll let it slide for old time's sake.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: By the way, the navigation system of the Volnov is on lockdown and not even I can turn it off. I suggest you send your men to stop it quickly, otherwise...

spans.text: By the way, the navigation system of the
is on lockdown and not even I can turn it off. I suggest you send your men to stop it quickly, otherwise...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Who knows what might happen?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Proshchay. Razin out.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: The second-floor deck is closest to open ground.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'll count myself lucky if I don't fall to my death. I wish I had listened when Oleg was telling me about those safe-fall positions.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Oh, screw it—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: 'Stand up, they say.'

a.text: He's going down to the end of the road, all in our name♪
Up until the second day when the sun shall rise again♪
Still we advance, draw our blades, cut down our foes♪
Still we bleed, fall to the floor, bury our dead with woe♪
Still, history pushes us, back onto our own blades we go♪
For those who passed through the darkness and saw the face of death♪
One more day the land shall live♪
One more day we will be free♪

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Hah... singing by myself is boring!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: In Baba's name, what I should really sing is—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Durak politics, durak death —

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Tupoi, Viy!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hierda... there you are. I've been looking all over the place for you.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why didn't you wait for me—*cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...I'm leaving, Anatoliy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I said, I'm leaving. I'm going to find my companions, whom I had entrusted to some people who could be trusted.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I should have been devoting myself to helping people who suffer...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What about me? What about me?!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Come with me, Anatoliy.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You will not find salvation here.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hah... yeah, of course! I stabbed my own mother because of you and that woman—because of what you said!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: No, it's not that. That was the right thing to do.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Your mother brought you pain, and brought war to the city, causing countless people to lose their homes. But your actions will bring life to even more.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You have atoned for your sins, Anatoliy. You have done well.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You—*cough*—ugh!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Anatoliy...
Hierda leans forward to examine the young man once more.
The yellow rocks have spread across his body, creating irregular lumps under his clothes.
It is the end for him.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What you think... doesn't matter anymore. Just...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Help me, one last time.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You can do it. Only you...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: But I don't want to, not anymore.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...Hierda?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: If this is to be your end, I will accept it. I don't want you to continue to devote yourself to a painful, meaningless life.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: This time, I won't help you anymore.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: It's almost ten. Everyone who walked in since nine-thirty was a noble.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Most of their faces are unfamiliar to me... but they aren't even trying to hide it, the way they behave themselves.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Has the time changed?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: No. I think they just decided they wouldn't bother to hide it anymore.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: We've reached the point where a show of force feels better than to continue to deceive the Tsar, as one might play pretend with a child.

steps.name: Concerned Noble
steps.text: Is the Duchess Volkina not here yet?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: The Central Army has not received any orders. The Capital Guard's assignments at the venue are within reasonable boundaries.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Perhaps she has chosen to stay on the sidelines, again.

steps.name: Concerned Noble
steps.text: As expected... five minutes until it starts. Let us go in, Vice Chairman.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: You go first... I'm waiting for someone.
Every seat in the hall is filled beneath the great dome of the State Council.
The ushers have led the attendees to their respective seats in an orderly manner, except—
The seats that should have been occupied by citizen's representatives from their respective raions are now occupied by taciturn nobles.
They wear neatly-ironed military uniforms or the latest fashion, wearing medals and luxurious fur shawls.
Clothes of every color surround skin and flesh, while the eyes follow the Tsar's steady steps.
No one stands, no one salutes. There's only a slow and stiff applause that seems intended to delay his speech.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: (Whispers) Sir, I have sent hands to check on the representatives—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Ensure their safety.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: (Whispers) I will. This is not unexpected. All you need to do is commit to pushing the Act through.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: (Whispers) The vote is simply a formality.
Fyodor nods wordlessly and passes Witte by, proceeding towards the podium on his own.
Suddenly, a young noble sitting in the front row stands up and salutes the Tsar with a smile.
All eyes are now upon this interlude.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: There is no need for formalities. This is a special day.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Sit down and watch.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty, we came because we heard about the 'citizen's forum' being held today.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I did not prohibit spectators.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Of course, though it seems Your Imperial Majesty has made a small mistake.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: We are not here as spectators. We are here as representatives of the 'citizens'.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: After all—
She gestures at the room full of nobles.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Are we not the most important citizens of Ursus?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Before you continue your grandstanding, return to your seat.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You are in my way.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Majesty—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: And if you claim to represent the 'citizens'...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Then hear what the citizens of the Empire of Ursus truly need now.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Are you ready, Vetochki?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I-I'm ready!

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Don't worry about not being heard. You may stutter a little bit, but you know exactly what you're saying.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You've already said it once in the Far North under fire. These people have no weapons, only their tongues.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: All you need to do is reveal the truth...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: To say what you truly want to say.

steps.name: Concerned Noble
steps.text: Has the one you were waiting for arrived?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: No, she hasn't...

steps.name: Concerned Noble
steps.text: Then perhaps she won't. As you said yourself, she may have chosen to stay on the sidelines again—

steps.name: Concerned Noble
steps.text: Ah, it's about to begin.
The Tsar unrolls a piece of paper.

In recent days, he has spent long hours consulting Witte and his other trusted advisors, scrutinized the details with the Supreme Court, and discussed with the citizens' representatives to arrive at the final draft that he is now holding.
Even he is surprised at how calm his voice is.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: On my way here, I saw fire pots set up along the roads to provide illumination at night.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Yet we all know that Deity Grypherburg had long stopped using oil lamps and bonfires to illuminate our streets, well before this became a nomadic city.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Perhaps the Grypherburg's nights are as they were a century ago, a situation that has carried on for two months.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: When the Originium mines closed, a once-affluent household in Grypherburg began burning furniture to stay warm.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: This was when I resolved to exploit the national Originium reserve, so we would not lose people to this harsh winter.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...Even that seems too little, too late.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Too late to prevent the Katorga Incident, and the reallocation of energy from Tsarevgrad to the residential districts can do little to stem the tide.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: This is a crisis on an unprecedented scale. It is not a temporary one, but one that threatens to wipe Ursus from the face of Terra, if no long-term solution is found.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act must be implemented.
Neither objection nor agreement, only silence.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...It is a provisional measure that will continue to be adjusted in practice, but it will at least save the people from the imminent plight of winter—

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: Does Your Imperial Majesty intend to nationalize the enterprises that we have worked so hard to build?

steps.name: Reserved Noble
steps.text: Or distribute the energy to the Armies in exchange for their obedience?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: No amount of industry and enterprise, no amount of territory will mean anything, if Ursus does not survive the winter.

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: In that case, why not simply read out the provisions and go straight to the vote?

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: Or have you decided that it is not worth the time to even go through the formalities, seeing our familiar faces?

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: (Whispers) Sir, message from Chairman Witte.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: (Whispers) About the original representatives... we just found out—
Fyodor's eyes widen as he sees the names on the piece of paper handed to him.
He frowns as he looks to the crowd.
All the whispering attendees have the same expression on them—one of scorn and mockery.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: (Whispers) I'm sorry, sir... we made a mistake. We should have discovered the swap sooner.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: (Whispers) Chairman Witte says that there's still a way to reschedule and hold a true citizen's forum, if you wish.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: ...Understood.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Speaking of familiar faces.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I'm sure you know that I have personally met with the elected citizen's representatives from the various raions, in order to make sure that the people's voices are heard.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Miners, grocers, pipeline workers, tutors, and other trades that I had never even heard of. New faces, all of them.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: It expanded my horizons and led me to reflect. I thought it was a beneficial thing, to learn about how the people live, to hear more about their real needs—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Only moments ago did I discover the truth.

steps.name: Concerned Noble
steps.text: (Whispers) Did we overdo it...?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: It was necessary.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The people I met with were not who they claimed to be. They were not miners, grocers, pipeline workers, or tutors.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: They were actors from rural theaters, secretaries of counts, minor nobles whose names occupy a place at the very end of the Almanac of Nobility, the idle sons of wealthy urbanites—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: It all makes sense now.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Their unusual eloquence, compromises reached so easily, and ill-fitting clothes riddled with holes in locations unrelated to labor...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Yet I did not realize at the time.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Perhaps it takes a fool to be fooled.

steps.name: Voice from the Door
steps.text: —No—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It is not so!

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: Who are you?!

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: How dare you intrude upon the council in session!

steps.name: Concerned Noble
steps.text: Wait, is she—
Upon seeing the face of the interloper, the nobles turn their heads to the Vice Chairman in the front row.
Vasily does not turn or respond to the countless eyes peering at him from behind.
His gaze is fixed on the Tsar on the podium, seemingly waiting for him to speak.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You...
Fyodor waves away the guards trying to stop the young woman.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What do you have to say?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It is not so, Your Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You are not a fool. If you have been deceived, it is only because there are arrogant traitors in our midst, trampling upon your dignity with their dishonor.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They are well-prepared, while you and those around you cannot be constantly watching them and their insidious plots.

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: Gorchikov! Tell your daughter to watch her tongue!

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: She's a grown woman. She's responsible for her own actions.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: You are... Eloysius Vasilyevna Gorchekova.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I am, Your Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I do not recognize the one with you. Who is she?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The true representative of the citizens.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: How do you prove that she is not an actor, like the ones on this list?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: She is a survivor of the Far North, one of the witnesses who should have testified against the Grand Duchess.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Anyone who heard that broadcast from the Far North will remember her voice.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: She and her fellow surviving miners should have been the representatives of Odoyev Raion.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The miners I saw—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I'm not sure you really saw any miners.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Why do you bring her here today?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What you should be asking is, what does she want?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What do you want, Vetochki?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: H-Hello. I-I'm Vetochki. My mother calls me, Anya.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I-I come from the, Far North, Mining District.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I-I want everyone, at the treatment center, to have a, warm bed.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I want, the Infected, to have a roof, over their heads.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I-I want more, people like us—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: To live through, the winter.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I want to, vote for... uh...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Y-Yes!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I want, to vote, so that people, won't die from, cold and illness.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: C-Can I?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Reserved Noble
steps.text: 'Of course,' Your Imperial Majesty? What guarantee can you make to this poor girl?

steps.name: Reserved Noble
steps.text: You see? Those 'citizens' you speak of do not know how to rule a nation. You may be demonstrating your benevolence and mercy by allowing them to participate, but you are not truly helping them.

steps.name: Reserved Noble
steps.text: Even this Act that you speak of is ultimately taking from one mouth to feed another. It cannot solve any of the major issues Ursus is facing.

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: Besides, is this a playground or a middle school? Are people allowed to just walk in, claim to be somebody, and start lecturing on the nation's future?

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: There is nothing we can do, if you wish to ram this Act through. However, you must know—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I know all about the consequences.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I thought that the enemy of the empire stood at the border of the Central Governorate.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: It seems I was wrong.
The Tsar slams the pile of papers in his hand on the podium.
He scans the room, at the myriad expressions in the crowd.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The enemy of the empire is here.

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: Majesty! I must remind you that your reckless decision may cause you to pay—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Take him away.

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: Majesty!

steps.name: Unhappy Noble
steps.text: Gorchikov! You coward! You and that spawn of yours will pay—
Soldiers quickly 'escort' the noble out of the hall, his shouts echoing in the corridor.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Anyone who wishes to go with him should do so now.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: If there are none, I shall proceed to the resolution.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Majesty—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Since those present are in agreement that the 'citizens' who comprise more than ninety percent of the empire's population do not deserve to have a voice...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: There is no need for a council that claims to represent these citizens.

steps.name: Reserved Noble
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty can't mean—

steps.name: Concerned Noble
steps.text: Gosudar...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act is hereby passed into law, effective immediately.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: In addition, as the Emperor and Autocrat of All the Ursines, I proclaim...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The entire legislature, both State Council and Imperial Duma...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: are hereby dissolved.
